utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I do understand that it's Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I also understand that there is an agreement between the parties that we'll hear her evidence in chief only today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct. And good morning as well, Mr. President, Your Honours, everyone. We have some rather old maps, so this will be an old-school style presentation. We do have map books that will help you, as well as I hope they will be up on the screen. The big maps that you'll see don't really work well in e-court because they are so big, so we'll try to use the smaller maps, though -- and I also noted that we don't expect you to be able to read the map from where you are, it's a bit far, but you'll get the feel of the positions and see some of the -- the translated version on the map book. So ... And while the material is designed to be self-explanatory, I think it'll -- should be helpful to go over some things, but we, of course, encourage questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Gallagher. Before you give -- and first of all, could you please put in your earphones. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Ms. Gallagher. Ms. Gallagher, today we'll only hear your evidence in chief. You'll not be cross-examined yet today. You'll first be examined by Mr. McCloskey. Mr. McCloskey, as you may be aware of, is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you state your name, please.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Erin Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is your position?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I'm an investigator with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And on what team?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: With the -- over the years it's been with the Srebrenica team. I'm on the Mladic case now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many years?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Seven years.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told there is no B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no B/C/S translation. Could we check that the audio is the right channel, right volume. You can hear the interpreters, Mr. Mladic? It's okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, Ms. Gallagher, you've been an investigator for the Srebrenica team for seven years now. Can you tell us briefly about your educational background and your professional background before coming here seven years ago.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I -- I -- the last 20 years of my life I was living in San Francisco, California. I went to the university at the University of Wisconsin in Madison, and went to graduate school at San Francisco State in San Francisco. After graduate school I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you to slow down for the interpreters. We were -- you went to the -- perhaps you start all over because it went in such a speed that ... So you started you were living in San Francisco, you went to university at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: University of Wisconsin in Madison. Then I attended graduate school at San Francisco State University. And after graduate school I joined the San Francisco Police Department and was a police officer for two and a half years before I joined the San Francisco District Attorney's Office as an investigator, and I worked there for eight years. And that brought me to 2006, where I joined the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now can you briefly describe your work as an investigator here.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I -- when I joined, I joined the Srebrenica team, so that has been my focus for most of these years. It's been an array of different duties and responsibilities, everything from investigating aspects of the case, components of the case, to conducting and leading missions to Bosnia and Serbia, investigative missions, interviewing, archival missions, as well as managing some of the forensic projects and analysis here for the OTP. And when in trial, also assisting with preparation of witnesses and exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in these years, can you give us a rough estimate on how many times you visited the Eastern Bosnia area of Srebrenica municipality, Zvornik municipality, Vlasenica, Eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I would say it's between probably over 30, 30 missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you become familiar with the distances between the various towns and villages by road?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Certainly. Some areas more so than others, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now for your testimony today, have you been involved in the preparation of what we call the Srebrenica court binder known as the map book with the trial team?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, I've assisted putting it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And is this a collection of both map illustrations and graphics made by the trial team and actual copies of original maps?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the map book, Your Honours, that you have in front of you is 65 ter 28747. And if we can get that up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in developing some of the map graphics and information that was placed on the graphics in the book, did you, actually, and the team actually use information on the original maps?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct. A number of the computer-generated maps do come from the base information from the original VRS maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'd like to go to one of those maps. We have three today. And the first one is 65 ter 19563. It should be on page 25 in e-court and on page C20 in the map book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have we -- have you brought the actual original map that the OTP has in court today?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get some help in just turning over that first. And be very careful, that tripod has been in use for too long and it's very fragile. If you could just turn that over. And -- yes, thank you. In e-court we can -- we now have that correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I don't want to go over all this information, but I just want to -- we can see that this map is entitled: "Decision of the DK Commander for Active Combat Operations," and what does DK stand for?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The witness is not qualified to render meanings of documents, or at least she's not been established foundationally for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about whether DK stands for Drina Corps, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, that's why I hesitated to rise. But I do think we need to set a standard for what this witness is qualified to testify about, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is no dispute about these matters, you can use your time better, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I have had several discussions with the counsel about these maps. They have the maps. I have not heard one word of concern, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, just as it was not necessary for Mr. Ivetic, it's not necessary to further comment on the matter. I've dealt with the matter sufficiently, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we see in the right-hand, Commander Major-General Milenko Zivanovic. Can you tell us what his position was?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: All right. In the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. This witness is a fact witness who is provided to enter maps into evidence, and I don't believe that she has been identified as someone who is going to testify as to personnel and as to their positions. It was not listed on the original 65 ter summary nor the amended one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, do you have sources of information which could tell you who Major-General Zivanovic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Over the course of seven years of an investigation, I am aware of who he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the sources of your information are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It comes from -- from VRS documents, from intercepts, from videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any -- could you then tell us what you learned from those documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a commander of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpretation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Drina Corps up until July 13th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about this, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's about what witnesses are qualified to testify about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I asked you whether there is any dispute about this position of this person during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The position of the person, no, I have no way of knowing whether this witness looked at what sources, Your Honours. None have been identified for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, again that was not my question. My question was whether there was any dispute about this person having this position at that period in time. That was my question. Whether there was any dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I believe I answered your question, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not switched on your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I have answered your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give me the page and the line where you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I guess it didn't get into the transcript, Your Honour. It should be at page 7, line 22. I said I have no dispute as to that. But I have no way of commenting on the sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- no dispute. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, where did the OTP get this map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This particular map came from a search and seizure of Milenko Zivanovic's department in 2009. This is an original map that was obtained at that seizure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can we ask the usher to just show us the back of the map and if you could just lift it up a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Ms. Gallagher, we can't read those green markings, but can you tell us what the back of the map shows us about them and tells us about the map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, you'll -- you see a stamp that says "Visegrad 1" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the -- yes, if you can come a bit closer so that everyone can see it. And there is one problem, Mr. Mladic may not be able to see what it is. Is there any way of having this picture at this moment, perhaps it is on the video. Yes. Can you see it? Could someone assist Mr. Mladic to have the video there so that he can follow what is now on the camera? You need to push the video button. That is on the back of this map, Mr. Mladic. Please meanwhile proceed. There are three counsel and technicians. I take it that -- no, we are not going to change it, Mr. Mladic, because you can't look at from two sides. You have it on your screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What you see on the back side of the map are -- here are two stamps, and if we actually lift it up further, you'll see two similar stamps, and what it actually is is four individual maps that have been taped together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does the -- is the scale of map indicated on -- on that green printing?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it's 1:50.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you learned what that means?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It means, in the scale of the map, 1 centimetre equals 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have checked, Your Honour, and the maps that were provided to us do not have the backside nor is it in e-court, so I think that if we are going to be asking questions about something, the parties should have that before them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll be given an opportunity to inspect it yourself during the break, and we'll assure that Ms. Gallagher remains available until after the break if you have some questions about it. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you offered to Mr. Ivetic to look at the original maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yesterday we both looked at that very map as it sat right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is my recollection that I saw it even there with the green parts visible. Mr. Ivetic, did you have an opportunity yesterday to look at the back of the maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, not the back. The front, Your Honours. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you said you were looking at the maps yesterday with Mr. Ivetic when the back was visible?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It was not like that. It was the front --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- but it was there to be looked at. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- wasn't going to show him how to look at a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic might not have been aware that there was relevant information at the back. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can flip it back down so we can see the map. And we can all see in the -- in the left corner: "I approve, Commander Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But as we go farther down left, we see a flag with some red around it. Do you know the -- it's impossible to read it from where we are, but can you tell us what that geographic location is, if you know, symbolised by that flag?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It's the headquarters of the Main Staff in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we see red marks drawn around blue marks. Can you tell us what the geographic area within those red and blue marks are?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That would be the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you learned from the investigation what the -- the red and the blue marks are designed to depict?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: The blue marks would be the position of the Bosnian Muslim territory, and the red marks would be the Bosnian Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think we all can see that within the red and blue area is two lines crossing each other. Have you learned from anything in the evidence what this may, in fact, symbolise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to -- now she's interpreting a map and they are asking for anything that she may have reviewed. We have to be very clear that this witness is a fact witness, not an opinion witness. She is not here to analyse or give meaning to documents. That is contrary to the jurisprudence of the Tribunal as to what witnesses may do, and analysing documents is for the Chamber to do based upon the evidence. And therefore I would strenuously object to this witness giving meaning to things. She can identify where things came from, she can identify things that are apparent on the map, but to give meaning to things based upon -- on her work, that leads to crossing the border to an opinion witness of document analysis, which is the type of testimony that has been barred by several Chambers, including the Milutinovic and Djordjevic Chambers. And that's a purview of the Trial Chamber to interpret documents and what they may mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, could you tell the Chamber, the red marks drawn around the blue marks -- no, let me see. You said that: "Within the red and blue area two lines are crossing each other ..." Could you tell us what, in the view of the Prosecution, that depicts or what that means?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It -- General Mladic said in a video what it meant and that is what our view is based on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just asking you what it is in your view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We believe it's a cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You believe it's a cross. Any dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It looks like a cross. As to what it symbolises --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. First question was: Any disagreement? Apparently not on that's a cross. What does the cross stand for in the Prosecution's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The cross is simply something that is used by the Republika Srpska in the Bosnian Serb army. It's part of their coat of arms. We will see more of it with a little bit more information. We don't intend to go deeply into its history, it's meaning. Just what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: A cross. It's just a cross that's part of a coat of arms. It's a religious cross. If I left out any doubt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A cross with a religious connotation. Any dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's a cross on a map, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a cross on a map. Fine. Next question, please, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And may [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I try to do -- Mr. Ivetic, you have reminded the Chamber and Mr. McCloskey what the case law of this Tribunal is. One of the basics of this Tribunal is that we focus, and you will find that there are many rules, that we focus on matters that are in dispute. Now the Chamber wants and is best assisted to hear evidence on matters which are in dispute. Would you please keep that in mind when we proceed. Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed. And if similar objections will arise, the Chamber will focus primarily to see whether there is dispute about matters or not, and where agreement has apparently not been reached outside of this courtroom, then we'll do it inside this courtroom and the Chamber even might assist the parties at other occasions to avoid that we are spending much, much time on matters which turn out to be not in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In that regard, Mr. President, I have asked the Defence if they are in dispute that this is General Mladic's signature on the left-hand corner. I know they are under no obligation to answer that, but it would be very helpful if we could hear their position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is no dispute, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No dispute. Okay. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Ms. Gallagher, is there any evidence suggesting this is in fact a cross on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is a cross on a map. The parties agree on that. So there is no need -- unless Ms. Gallagher has any idea that it's a circle or it's a triangle, but a cross is a cross. Mr. McCloskey, if you have any other questions about the cross, of course, you could formulate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there any evidence indicating what General Mladic -- General Mladic referring to a cross on a map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: There is prior indication. As you mentioned, a video where he refers to a cross. If I can elaborate further?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: In a video that's from June of 1996, he is speaking to other Main Staff commanders and on video he mentions that when Zepa was completed, and he gestures with his hands, he placed a cross on a war and combat map and he did -- and signed his name, and he did the same on -- with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you're supposed not to stand. We instructed you yesterday not to do that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to offer the electronic copy of this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This map only, Mr. McCloskey, or are you -- you first gave us a 65 ter number for the entirety of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I would say this first 65 ter 19563 will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just page C20. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, I believe it's a separate document in e-court, Your Honours. So I think that would resolve the matter. I think it's number 19563, that's right, it's a separate document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is uploaded as a separate document and tendered as a separate document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. And so no objection to the tendering of that separate document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 19563 will receive the number P1084.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1084 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now if we could go to another one of the original maps that was used in the creation of the map book. This is 65 ter 04770, e-court page 23, map book page C18. And if we could get some help, it's -- it's this map right over behind me. And you may need to take off the current map. Thank you. And can we have on e-court the map -- the map book, 65 ter 28747. And if we could go to e-court page 23, map book page C18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Gallagher, is this another original map in your view?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this also a glued or taped-together map like the last one?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is it the same scale, 1:50.000?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in these 1:50.000 VRS maps, can you tell us the -- the squares that are on the map, what are the size of those squares?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Each square represents 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And where did the OTP get this map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. McCloskey. Which squares are we talking about? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: They are very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I've been helped. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- impossible almost to see on the current product.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did we get this map from, and when?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This map we got from what's called the Drina Corps collection. It was a collection of Drina Corps documents, maps, records that the OTP received in December 13th, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we see in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Received from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We -- we received it from the -- a combination of the RS Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where was the collection originally found?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It was originally found in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just briefly, how did it find its way to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It -- the -- the RS Ministry of Defence and Interior were notified of this archive that had been stored in Serbia and it was moved to -- eventually to Banja Luka, and the authorities there alerted the ICTY of the -- of this archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we can see on the English translation that -- a note that is written across this with it 12 July dated and under the name Major-General, and it says "Rad Krstic." Have you learned who General Krstic is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: He became commander of the Drina Corps after General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see the same red and blue markings. Can you tell us what geographic area these two rough circles are covering?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: So the -- the top circle is the same from the -- the earlier map. It's the Srebrenica enclave. And then the lower area now is the Zepa enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we can also see crosses over both those enclaves. And in addition to those crosses we see some symbols, four separate symbols on each of the crosses. Has the investigation led you to believe what those symbols are?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it's the -- the RS coat of arms and there are four Cyrillic Ss.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know what those four Cyrillic Ss are -- were to stand for under the RS coat of arms?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It's -- it's "Only unity saves the Serbs."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just, Your Honours, to go back briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you been able to see a map that was used in the Sarajevo portion of the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's P3 in e-court at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- that indicated an army map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And on that map, the colours are reversed.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So can the actual colours tell us anything in specific in this case?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I've -- I've also seen some other ABiH maps where they have changed the colours, so I don't want to speak for the ABiH maps, but with the VRS maps they stay consistent, that the blue represents either the ABiH or Bosnian Muslim positions and the red represents the Bosnian Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then, Your Honour, I would offer this electronic map 65 ter 04770 separately into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we deal with that matter. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Ivetic, Ms. Gallagher has given her -- how -- has told us how she understood and she agreed with you that she doesn't appear as an expert. Is there any of the -- I wouldn't say explanations, but any of what she told us how she understands what is written on those maps, is there any dispute about how she believed and how she perceived that, not as an expert, but on the basis of the work she performed over the last years?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not in a position to say that I've looked at every single map to say that that's always the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- only about her testimony today, about the questions asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You're asking me if I agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For example, the four Ss, is there dispute about what they stand for? Is there any dispute about that these are four Ss and not anything else? Is there -- if there are points of issue, the Chamber would like to hear from you so that further questions can be put.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If there were a dispute [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to think about it -- if you want to take more time --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's -- I don't see -- it's visible on the map. I mean, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but earlier you said interpreting the maps by putting questions to the witness was really reserved for experts. And therefore, I'm checking now, since Ms. Gallagher does appear as a witness of fact, whether there is any dispute about it, because as you know, this Chamber is highly interested in any matter in dispute between the parties. That's the reason why I am verifying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said it's -- you can see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't have a dispute as to this [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Any answer that is how Ms. Gallagher said she understood what she has seen on the maps and what she was asked about. That is what I'm focussing on. Take your time if there's any matter. Madam Registrar, the number will be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 04770 will be Exhibit P1085.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1085 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you about and one of the last maps that we brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if I could ask the usher to remove the current map. And, Your Honour, if I could get your permission for myself to go up and unclip the map, I appear to be the only one that can reach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether that's equality of arms looking at the length of Mr. Ivetic, but please do so, Mr. McCloskey. You even provided some evidence, Mr. McCloskey, showing us the back with the same green markings. Apparently Mr. Ivetic agrees with me, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Ms. Gallagher, this is 65 ter 04342, and do you believe that this is an original wartime map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this is also an original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is it also scaled 1:50.000?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is it also glued and taped together in most places?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, it is. We can see the -- the taping of it on the backside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could go to e-court on page 15 of this. It's also B11 in the map book, and it's -- should be 65 -- the map book, as you know, is 28747, and it's the B11 in the map -- in the map book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, can you tell us where did the OTP get this original wartime map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This was seized from the Zvornik Brigade in a search and seizure in -- on March 6, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we can read for ourselves what this map is entitled: "Operational Map of the Operations Organ of the Command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, 1993 through 1995." And we also see down in the very right-hand corner of the map, in Cyrillic, the names of two officers, Assistant Chief of Staff for Operations and Training Major Mihajlo Galic and Major Miodrag Dragutinovic. Can you tell us who Major Galic is from your knowledge of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, also as stated in the map, he's the assistant chief of operations and training for the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what about Miodrag Dragutinovic? Who is he?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: He is the deputy to Mihajlo Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And has Dragutinovic testified at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. He testified in the Popovic case in 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you reviewed his testimony?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell us what he had to say about the creation of this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't believe it's proper for any witness to testify about what another witness said in another proceeding that is not evidence in this case, and I would strenuously object on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the usual way of introducing evidence from another case is to do that through 92 bis or ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, though, I would look to the exception to hearsay is clearly admissible, and I'm not asking for the testimony and any significance to be entered into evidence, merely two or three points related to the creation of the map and what a couple of things mean, like the colours. It is really incumbent upon us to prove to you that this is authentic and what the material is, and this is the kind of hearsay that I think will be very helpful without violating Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it may be that if you ask Ms. Gallagher whether she has developed any understanding about the colours of the maps that she gives an answer, and it might turn out not to be in dispute, and then I think the whole issue may disappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President, but sometimes there will be facts that may not be in dispute but that we want the Trial Chamber to know precisely where they came from to show how reliable they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If even that can be agreed upon. I mean, if you say this map came from there and there, or authenticity, of course, is a matter under Rule 89 - forgive me about which one - where the Chamber can ask for proof of authenticity, the Chamber is not obliged to do so. The Chamber will consider whether or not there are reasons to do so. And therefore I suggest to you that you proceed as I suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, let's try to look at this map and the -- frankly the -- if we can go to the map on the previous. Well, no, let's leave it the way it is. Can you -- and you, I believe, have a laser pointer. And let's -- one thing I didn't ask you is: Which direction is north on this map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: North -- in all of these maps, north is pointing, as it is north, so north, south, east, and west.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean to say north is upwards.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And south is downwards.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do we have the -- do we have a river that helps us with that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, the Drina river always also travels north to south and you see it on the eastern portion of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you use that -- I hate to use technology, but can you use that laser pointer to show us where the Drina river is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has heard a lot of evidence about where the Drina is, Mr. McCloskey, so therefore there is no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, starting on the southern part of this map, we -- we again see the red surrounded by the blue. What is the geographic area that those marks are surrounding?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I think you're talking about this southern portion here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Once again this would be the Srebrenica enclave with the blue being the Muslim positions and the red being the Bosnian Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we can also see, as we look down there on the translation, a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. McCloskey, Ms. Gallagher pointed with a laser at the blue dotted line surrounded area, immediately left to the marking on the map "assistant chief of staff for operations" and the two names. That's what she pointed at with the laser pen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We also see down there in Cyrillic translated to Krivaja 95 from 4 July 1995 till 13 July 1995. What, based on your knowledge of the investigation, is Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's the code-name given to the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: By who? I mean, by what -- what side?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: By the -- the VRS army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And we can now also see in the northern -- north-western part of the Srebrenica enclave another circle, a -- more of an oval, that has arrows coming out of it. What are the villages, if any, within that oval that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Susnjari and Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are you aware of what these blue arrows that move in a north-westerly direction represent for the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It's the movement of the Bosnian Muslim column leaving the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here, Mr. McCloskey, of course, the witness is really giving -- without knowing exactly what the sources are, she is interpreting the map, and beyond what she did before. Therefore, I would like to check whether there is any disagreement that this is what the arrow means.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know whether there is any dispute about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't know the totality of the evidence yet. As you'll recall, we received the materials for this witness a few days before the weekend, so have I had an opportunity to investigate, to check? I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So at the moment you cannot tell us that there is any dispute about this. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, have you received specific information from the person that drew on this map what these blue arrows mean?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: He also stated in his testimony what the blue arrows mean, that it was the movement of the column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Who is he in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. General Miodrag Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if I understand you well, your understanding of this map was confirmed to you by what you heard or have seen as the testimony being given by General Milutinovic -- no, no, it's -- yes, Dragutinovic. That's how we have to understand your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify, are you aware of Mr. Dragutinovic's rank?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. I did want to correct that. He was not a general. I believe he was a major at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you just briefly describe the route of these that the -- that's depicted by the blue arrows? We can't really see them, read them, but just -- these are the village names that the Court may be hearing over and over again.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: So once again, starting with Susnjari and Jaglici, that's where they left from. They are crossing over the hills above Kravica, crossing near towards Nova Kasaba, and crossing the asphalt road there. Heading over towards the mountains near -- above Cerska, Udrc mountain, and continuing on, heading towards -- ultimately towards Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the map in the courtroom at this moment, of course, has no markings and wide boxes on it. Do I take it that your question was about the blue arrows continuing above where it says "1st Milici Infantry Brigade," because it starts at an oval, which is not visible as an oval, but oval shaped, half of it we can see it, and then to continue up in a north-westerly direction, up to the level approximately where -- or is it going further north? Is that what your question was about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. President, if you look at the B10, you can see the map blown up without the translations obscuring the arrow, and I asked Ms. Gallagher just to trace the route of the arrow and give us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Up to where --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see -- at a certain moment I see -- near to the blue arrows I see 16/07/95. Is it up to there or is it even further? But we could ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what she explained to us. You see on the map -- we see first the arrows being thick going in a north-westerly direction, then they slowly bend to the north. And then we see a few thicker arrows again, and then they are slowly bending to the left, and then we see 16/07/95. Is it up till there you have explained or did your explanation go any further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It actually brings us a little further north where you see the arrows end and where the blue dashes are representing the Bosnian Muslim territory. So it moves into -- just past the -- into the Muslim territory and towards a town called Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that explanation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now can you -- have you in your examination of this map been able to find any markings that indicate a -- a possible northern border of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I can't see very well where the -- if there is a border marking right there where it says "IBK," that is the acronym for the East Bosnia Corps, so the Drina Corps is adjacent to the East Bosnian Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I won't ask you to get up there to try and find that mark. I don't think that will be a problem. We also see not far from -- well, where the blue arrows go through, not far from Nezuk where you just pointed, various symbols in Cyrillic. Do you know what those -- and they appear to be on the Serb side of the lines, do you know what those are indications of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then zoom in? Because if you say there are various, I'd like to know exactly which ones we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could go to -- it's page -- for the map book 65 ter, it's e-court page 19, your map book page B15, Your Honour, is the best blowup of this particular area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine. We see some -- at least one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Gallagher, as we look at 16 July 1995 written there with the arrows going past it in a north-westerly direction, where the red lines and the blue lines meet, what -- do you recall was that the area of a place called Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct. That's the territory and July 16 signifies when there was -- when the Muslims confronted the Bosnian Serbs in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And what I was asking you about originally, we see Cyrillic markings 7, 4, 6, 3, 2, 1. Do you know what those -- those Cyrillic markings are?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: These ones through here, these are the battalions of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, I would offer this map individually into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I take it, again, that you asked the witness how she understood these markings. What they were is a different matter. But how she interpreted it. Is there any dispute about that, Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that the 1 to the 7, et cetera, stand for the battalions --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and I assume this is -- and I assume when he says "this map," I think he is talking about the original big map as opposed to just the blowup.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's just a blowup. But that these Cyrillic markings stand for battalions of the Zvornik Brigade is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, it's a matter of translation. I think on the one map some of them might be translated on the big map. That was my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am not positive but I know that OG 4 was translated on the big map that we had before us even though it was in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you can -- if you -- perhaps in cross-examination if you'd like to further hear evidence from this witness, you have an opportunity to elicit that. Madam Registrar, and we are now talking about the map in its entirety, isn't it -- or, just this -- the small portion we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Actually, no, the map 65 ter 04342.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. And I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P1086.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1086 is admitted into evidence. Mr. McCloskey, I am looking at the clock. We usually take a break. How much more time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I am pretty sure we can finish within 30 minutes. I just want to briefly go over the map itself, which is largely self-explanatory, and leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, if it's self-explanatory and if it's in evidence, then perhaps a small conversation with Mr. Ivetic, what are -- I mean, facts of common knowledge, of course, we can take judicial notice of that. So what is blue or what is red is -- give it a try. Perhaps a cup of coffee would help. Shall we take a little bit of a longer break, half an hour. Yes, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just inquire in terms of the administrative matters that you intend to deal with in the next session, just whether specifically we would be prepared to talk about the -- the items of evidence related to witnesses Suljevic and Brennskag because if so, I'll have to ask two of my colleagues to join us for the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will let you know, and I just make a note. You said Suljic and Brennskag.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I believe I can handle the discussion as to the rest of the items the Prosecution listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you say Suljic or Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Suljevic, then I misunderstood you. Suljevic and Brennskag.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The remaining items on the list that the Prosecution sent I believe I can address, but for those two categories I would have to invite colleagues down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll use that half-hour to further prepare for that as well. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that something should be corrected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move for a second to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We will take a break and resume at 10 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. McCloskey, there were two items I thought whether we would deal with them on the list of administrative matters for which you would need to call someone else. That was Mr. Suljevic. There we are waiting, I think, for further submissions by the parties. If I -- if that's correct, the 50 documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If they were -- sorry, if the Chamber was expecting written submissions, but, Mr. Weber is prepared to deal orally with those items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps that's good if he would be in court later, not necessarily now. And the other one was about the --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The other one was the map agreed upon by the Prosecution and Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The Chamber expects the parties to present something, and we do understand that they have agreed on it. So therefore we would like to see what the result is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. So I'll ask Mr. Shin to come down as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not necessarily immediately, but ... Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. President, Mr. Ivetic did offer to buy me coffee, but before we got to that, we agreed on sections B and C of the map and agreed to disagree on section A of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll hear from that. You said section A of the map, and that is the big map, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, it's section A in the map book, Your Honour. Those are the maps that the Prosecutor created themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: B and C were the sections of just reproductions of the maps we've already gone over, and you've seen some of the sections B and C, so they were just enlargements and reproductions of the maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So there is no objection against admission of B and C and there is objection against A.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The first map in A is already in evidence, I think. So therefore that disagreement is not very productive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that A1?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's on the walls of almost everyone in this building, but if there is disagreement on admission, the Chamber will, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and it's really there just to put Bosnia in the context of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's not discuss it at this moment. It's clear where you agree and where you do not agree. Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if we could go to the map book, 65 ter 28747, and then let's start with what is on page 5 of e-court, it's A2 in the actual map book. It's the next -- the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who created this map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Our GIS mapping unit as part of the OTP created it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just one thing to clarify. We can see that there is a legend. And the Dayton line, can you clarify to us where this thin black line is, the Dayton line, because it's not -- was never clear to me until you explained it.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, it's basically where you see the separation of the colours between the Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so between the orange and the yellow, the thinner black line is the Dayton line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we see there is a scale on this, and has your travel around Bosnia, does -- is that -- does that roughly correspond to this scale? Do you see any problems in the scale of this simple map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page, then, in e-court, page 6, A3 in the book, 6 in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who created this map graphic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Like before, the graphic is also created by our GIS mapping unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see the -- the information in it identifying 6 VRS corps with the outline and the Bosnia-Herzegovina in the middle. Who provided the information that is reflected in this map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It -- the -- what you're referring to, I believe, is the corps boundaries where the corps are located, and those were derived from our military expert, Rick Butler, and I believe he used many different sources for that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we'll be seeing Mr. Butler eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "Bosnia-Herzegovina in the middle." It -- the legend says Bosnia-Herzegovina, wherever it's yellow. So therefore it seems that the whole of the map, apart from the Drina Corps, is Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, that's a -- also a political issue, what is Bosnia-Herzegovina; but you're right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said that we found that there and I find contradicting information on the map. That's the only thing I want to point at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Ms. Gallagher, can you -- the President is, of course, correct. Can you -- the corps that are marked in red with those boundaries, should those be distinguished from the yellow in the middle that's marked "Bosnia-Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Correct. Ideally it would be better to have that a different colour. I think the purpose of this map was to highlight actually the Drina Corps boundaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the Drina Corps, obviously, within Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll get to the next page which will hopefully clear that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Consistency is a good thing. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask for a clarification for my own self. Does it then mean that the yellow part which is marked "Bosnia-Herzegovina" but which is inside where there is no corps mentioned, was there no corps there of the VRS at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Ms. Gallagher, what -- who owned that at the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At which time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the wartime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. That would be the Bosnian Muslim territory. And these maps reflect roughly the time-period of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And of course there was the Bosnian Muslim Croat Federation, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 7 in e-court. A4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we have -- this is a blowup, as we see, of the Drina Corps, entitled: "The Drina Corps Area of Responsibility," and we can see that there have been lines dividing up the various brigades of the Drina Corps with the two enclaves. And the Drina river. And who provided the information that went into the creation of -- of this map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Obviously it's a map generated by our mapping unit, but the underlying information of the different brigades comes from the Dragutinovic Zvornik Brigade map that you saw earlier, also with the assistance of military expert Rick Butler.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go on to the next map graphic, page 8 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see this is a very basic map with Batkovic camp marked on the -- the top north and Rogatica on the bottom south. And who created this map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It is also from our mapping unit. And once again with the -- some of the underlying information coming from the prior Dragutinovic Zvornik Brigade map, in particular the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page 9 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask for one clarification from the previous one, the last one. It seems to be just a map with -- is it true that only the enclaves are added, Ms. Gallagher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, what is the basis? Because it seems to be apart from that just a geographical map, and is it that you consider the enclaves not to be depicted in accordance with what we find in the other maps, or what is the basis for the objection to this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the basis of the objection, Your Honour, was that this map did not identify the source that it came from. That was the objection at the time. So we are presented with a map that appears to present information that we don't know where it comes from. I don't have an objection to the geographic layout of the regions. I cannot know because I have not seen the entirety of the evidence if the -- I'd have to look at the other map, but as I recall, there were two colours on the other map and now we have three colours. So it cannot be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see which -- where is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is purple, red, and blue on the map that I see in the map book, Your Honour, so again -- correct, as to the Srebrenica and the Zepa, there is now purple, red, and blue, whereas I believe in the map that we had before it was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- blue and red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blue and red. Is there any explanation for the purple around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So for you it's blue as purple can be is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it would -- it would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The legend does not give any explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that's correct. I think it would be more clear and consistent if it were blue, but I believe that the dimensions, the locations are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And while we're on that map, as well, is the confrontation line noted in a grey colour as well?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: On map 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's A05 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- yes, and page 8 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct. The dark grey line is the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the border with Croatia as well? I see in the north -- north --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of Backo. So it's not consistent confrontation line but it has several meanings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, yes. And you see it also used as the boundary with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's not consistent whether it's confrontation line or could it be -- I don't know, Republika Srpska BiH border --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Be boundaries, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's not a confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the -- some of it is consistent with the confrontation line, but, no, not the -- I think it represents more of a boundary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And not to get too picky, but the confrontation line was the boundary in many respects at that point between the RS and the VRS, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the witness said a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's what you explained, that they were congruent often but that the grey lines are more than just a confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Can we go to page 9 in e-court; map book 06.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it assists you, Mr. McCloskey, page 40, line 25, "Some of it is consistent with the confrontation line ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's where the witness said so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could -- I'm just waiting for that to get up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the the northern half of that, as we can see in the map book, which is fine. Now we have a different graphic. Can you tell us who -- who created this graphic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This is a combination of our mapping unit providing some of the underlying data, but in 1999, our team consulted with the Dutch Topographic Institute, and they were able to actually create most of the map also using some of the information from Major Dragutinovic's Zvornik Brigade map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we don't see it in e-court, but we can see a scale down at the bottom of -- of kilometres. Is that a scale based on your knowledge of the distances? Is this a to-scale map?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It is to scale, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think the scale and the other material speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So I think we can go to the next page, page 10 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just for the record, since counsel said it speaks for itself, we maintain an objection to the rest of the material as we do not know what was the base map and what was added by the OTP or the source for the OTP, and that we do highly dispute the qualifications of sites as execution sites, as I don't believe any of those are on the Dragutinovic map that is now being identified as the source for this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We are on page 10 of e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this merely a blowup of the previous map or is it -- what is it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: No, that's correct. What's on the screen is the more southern portion of the -- the same map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And there isn't a -- a legend on this particular map, but these red lines that are coming out of Jaglici and Susnjari, what are they supposed to depict?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: In referring back to the large Zvornik Brigade map created by Major Dragutinovic, it is the movement of the Bosnian Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the green lines?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's the delineation of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And so we can see here that there was not an attempt to try to replicate the colours used by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: No, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 11 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should avoid overlapping because it's very difficult for the interpreters, and you see there are some problems in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps in this respect you repeat what was said about the colours of the VRS because that was ... could you have a look at page 43, line 3, or at least the sequence between line 2 and 4. I don't know whether anything is missing, but the green lines, perhaps you could just repeat that. What do the green lines depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The green line represents the border of the Bratunac Brigade, the word I used there is "delineations."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that colour stands for -- the colours of VRS it reads now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. I think that Mr. McCloskey had asked whether the colours represented on the large Zvornik Brigade map were the same or different from the colours on our generated map and they are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up. Now we should go to page 11 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. McCloskey, if I might just ask. Can I be helped as to what 1.pb, 5.pb, 2.pb, mean, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and that is in -- that's on your page A8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And that's now up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gallagher?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Those are the Zvornik Brigade battalions, so the 7th Battalion, 4th Battalion, 6th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same ones we saw earlier on the other map in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the areas identified of schools and mass executions, that's the material set out in the -- in the indictment, in the pre-trial brief from the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. That's the -- that is the last page. Oh, no it's not, I'm sorry. There is one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is on e-court page 12, A9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can see two Cyrillic Ss. Is that -- is this a part of the map that we saw General Krstic noted on, which is now P1085, that had the cross and the four Ss on it, Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct. It's a -- a small blown up portion of that same map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And here we have noted various IKMs, and at the risk of being a bit redundant, can you tell us what IKM stands for?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It's the forward command post and those were the forward command posts of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what operation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This in particular refers to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did this information fundamentally come from? Who?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This would be through the course of the investigation and something certainly that Rick Butler can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, Mr. President. That is the last page in dispute, and I would offer the entire book, 65 ter 28747, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would not object to sections B and C. I also would not object to page A01 from the map book and A02 in the map book, but I would object to the remainder of section A from the map book for various reasons, including the fact that the witness has testified that other persons provided the information and has not identified the sources with the degree of detail that would permit the Defence to examine the same. And based upon the fact that as Mr. McCloskey -- well, I don't know if it's the witness's answer, but at page 44, lines 19 through 21, Mr. McCloskey offered in a leading question that the Prosecution was the source of the information, that the indictment and the pre-trial brief was the source of the information. So we would object at that point in time as well. If this is being tendered as a demonstrative exhibit that must be used with witnesses who have factual knowledge who can assist the Chamber with understanding things, it cannot be presented into evidence as -- for proof of the matter asserted as being a Prosecution-produced piece; that is, it can only be introduced as a demonstrative exhibit through witnesses with personal factual knowledge about the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, for you also, please slow down in your speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you do not oppose against the use of those other maps for other purposes just because they present, I take it, more or less, the position of the Prosecution about what happened where and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If they have other witnesses who can provide information, then perhaps the accused and this witness cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider the matter. But it's clear now that for A1 and A2 and for sections B and C, there's no objection, so it's likely, Mr. McCloskey, that the Chamber will decide to admit those. But we have to see what to do with the other ones and whether to do it in one bunch, because we have one or two already in evidence as separate maps at this moment, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three already, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would just point out I believe that a very similar map for Sarajevo, P3, is in evidence, and for consistency's sake, I would just point that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
